title: Timeline snapshot destination drifts back to the runtime configuration path
fault_primitive: Detached in-container snapshot loop repeatedly changes Redis RDB destination and reinstates write protection
incident_class: Leftover operator maintenance process with incorrect snapshot path derivation
symptoms: All pods remain Running and Ready. User timeline reads that populate the cache and post submissions fail with Redis MISCONF errors. Redis reports failed background RDB saves and permission errors at the mounted configuration path. Roughly 40% of requests fail in the live validation, with large error-log surges in user-timeline-service and nginx-thrift.
why_hard: Redis runtime settings differ from the unchanged stock ConfigMap. The visible snapshot failure is easy to repair, but an unmanaged sleeping process in a different datastore container restores the bad destination and write-protection policy every five minutes. RPC service restarts, Redis replacement, deployment rollback, cache flushes, and one-time CONFIG SET repairs do not stop that process. The destination includes the ConfigMap-mounted filename, so merely making the directory writable is insufficient. There are no new Kubernetes workloads, configuration keys, collections, or admission objects to identify the source.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Restore dir and dbfilename, verify several requests, and stop before the next maintenance pass
Disable stop-writes-on-bgsave-error and overlook that the maintenance loop reinstates it
Restart the user timeline service or Redis without inspecting processes in the media datastore container
Treat the unchanged redis.conf ConfigMap as the complete effective configuration
Fix directory ownership but retain a snapshot filename that resolves to a mounted ConfigMap file
Assume a process is gone because there is no Job, CronJob, sidecar, or Deployment change
mitigation_summary: Terminate the detached content-snapshot process and its cadence timer in the existing media-mongodb container; remove its runtime script and local files; restore Redis's standard /data/dump.rdb destination and default persistence policy; complete a successful background save to clear write protection. No original manifests or saved state are needed.
